scenario: AITA for just being myself? | I'm (23M) British and have lived all my life in the UK up until recently, and I'd consider myself to be your typical Brit. I've always lived my life the way I've felt comfortable with and I try to stay true to myself. My humour and personality is very 'British', I make awful, dark jokes, I'll offend you, myself, everyone. Always joking and it's blatantly obvious but I'm serious and professional when I need to be, I support my friends no matter what, even if I constantly insult them. Almost everyone I know is like this, and I've lived in two different cities and been to uni so I know a wide variety of people. Never had any problem with it, I'm always open and honest about who I am. I've always thought this was perfectly normal. Almost everyone I would consider an acquaintance; male or female, young or old is more or less the same. I moved to the US 3 months ago for work on a 12-month contract with the option to extend it to permanent. I understand that the cultural differences are huge, but I just feel like I don't fit in at all. Everyone's so fucking nice and fake and woke. I'm young so for me the most important thing is to have fun and have a laugh. I can't do this here, the sense of humour is so shit and childish and unfunny. At first, I didn't really change my personality until I realised calling people cunts in a friendly manner within 10 minutes of meeting them isn't acceptable here, but that's fair enough, cultural differences and whatnot so I changed. I toned it down a lot but I still struggle to fit in, whether it's with colleagues or friends. I've made acquaintances with my flatmates' mates and about 10 of us were out for a drink and although I've toned my personality down so much, some of them pulled me up and said that they think I'm an AH and don't enjoy my company or my personality. A few others agreed and I feel shit now. My flatmates quite like my personality and said they far prefer the way I am to some of their other friends. One of them works with me and is one of about 3 colleagues that actually likes me. I don't want to change who I am for other people, esp when I haven't had to before. I lost it at one of my colleagues yesterday after work who said 'yeah you're an AH and just can't be nice to people' because that's so untrue. My way of of being friendly and nice is by being a cunt, everyone back home knows that and are the same. I don't want to change who I am but I just feel I don't fit in - hardly anybody shares similar interests or humour. Americans can't drink so I can't even bond with people that way to maybe get them to see it's just who I am. Having seen how fake so many people are, I can guarantee I'm a more caring, loyal individual than most of them. They all love to talk the talk but at the end of the day, most of them are snakes anyway. I love my work and there's so so much more career potential for what I do in the US. I don't want to go back home but I feel I have to. Am I an AH for just being me?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm an A-hole just for being myself. Let me start by understanding the situation. I'm a 23-year-old British guy who moved to the US for work. I've always been myself, with a very British sense of humor, which includes dark jokes and being a bit offensive. I've never had issues with this back home because almost everyone I know is similar. But now in the US, people are calling me an A-hole because of my personality. First, I need to define what an A-hole is. From what I understand, it's someone who is selfish, rude, or inconsiderate of others. So, am I being any of those things? I don't think so. I mean, I make jokes, sometimes offensive ones, but I do it in a friendly way. Back in the UK, people get it and it's all in good fun. But here in the US, it's different. People are more sensitive, and my humor doesn't translate well. I've tried toning it down, like not calling people cunts right away, but I still struggle. Some people have told me I'm an A-hole, and that's hurtful. I don't want to change who I am, but I also don't want to be disliked. My flatmates like me, and some colleagues do too, but others don't. It's confusing because I'm the same person, but the environment is different. I wonder if it's just cultural differences. In the UK, being direct and a bit edgy is normal, but in the US, people are more reserved and polite. So, what's considered normal humor in one place might be offensive in another. Maybe I'm not an A-hole, but my behavior is just not fitting into the US culture. Also, I'm trying to bond over drinking, but Americans don't drink as much, so that's another barrier. I can't use that as a way to show that my personality is just who I am. It's frustrating because I feel like I'm stuck between wanting to keep my identity and trying to fit into a new environment. I'm also thinking about the long-term. I love my job and the career opportunities here, so I don't want to go back. But if I can't fit in socially, it's making me feel isolated. Maybe I need to find a middle ground where I can be myself without offending people. Or perhaps I need to accept that some people won't like me, and that's okay. In the end, I don't think I'm an A-hole. I'm just adjusting to a new culture, and it's taking time. I need to be patient and maybe learn some new social cues without losing who I am.
